title: Reserves and Settlement Schedule: What a Claim Payment Is Measured From
content:
What the host's payout account holds in reserve, and the schedule that account settles on, decide what a payment on a Keyturn Host Protection Plan claim is measured from.

- Where what stands owed to the host is more than the reserves held on their payout account and that account settles on the marketplace's express or instant schedule, the payment is measured as the reserves held on the account.
- Where what stands owed is more than those reserves and the account settles on any other schedule, the payment is measured as what stands owed taken at the marketplace's part-settlement share of 60 percent.
- Where what stands owed is no more than those reserves, the payment is measured as the whole of what stands owed.

### A worked case (hypothetical figures)

Suppose 5000 stands owed to the host and the account holds 2000 in reserve.

| Schedule the account settles on | Payment measured at |
|---|---|
| Keyturn Express Payout Schedule | 2000.00, the reserves held |
| Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule | 2000.00, the reserves held |
| Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule, or any other | 3000.00, being 60 percent of what stands owed |

Where the reserves stood at 6000 instead, what stands owed is no more than they are, and the payment is measured at the whole 5000.00 on any schedule, express and instant included.

### The records behind the reading

The reserves held and the schedule the account settles on are read from the host's Keyturn Host Payout Account, the express and instant schedules being the Keyturn Express Payout Schedule and the Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule.
